ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, there is an isosceles right-angled triangle board, its hypotenuse $BC=8\, \text{cm}$. Inside it, $\triangle DEF$ has its sides parallel to the sides of $OABC$ respectively, and its hypotenuse $EF=4\, \text{cm}$. What is the ratio of the area of $\triangle DEF$ to the area of the shaded part?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution.} Given by the problem, we have: $\frac{S_{\triangle DEF}}{S_{\triangle ABC}}=\left(\frac{EF}{BC}\right)^2=\left(\frac{4}{8}\right)^2=\frac{1}{4}$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{S_{\triangle DEF}}{S_{\text{shaded area}}}=\frac{1}{3}$,\\
that is, the ratio of the area of $\triangle DEF$ to the area of the shaded portion is $\boxed{1\colon 3}$.
